note: Machine-readable mechanic map. One entry per analysed mechanic so a future agent does not have to rediscover the codebase. Line ranges verified against the tree at the time of writing; re-verify with grep before relying on them. Companions: MECHANIC_FINDINGS.md (report), MECHANIC_ATLAS.html (interactive). Analysed so far: budget, trade. Amended after an adversarial verification pass: the 'protectionism protects industry' reading was WRONG and has been corrected.

mechanics.one_line: Weekly closing of nation.gold plus the nine policy dials that steer it; owns the dials, collects everything else.
mechanics.structural_fact: TWO parallel accounting objects both write nation.gold: nation.budget (cities.js nationBudget, crown gold + army wages + administration) and nation.economy (fiscalBalance, taxes + tariffs + social + construction + debt). updateLedger re-imports three lines from the first into the second so the screen shows one statement.

measurements.protocol: scripts/audit/harness.mjs; process-isolated scenarios; seeds ix-a/ix-b/ix-c; warmup 60 weeks as AI then 260 measured weeks as player; wars suppressed unless noted; lever re-applied weekly; medians reported
measurements.control_integrity: PASS - every dial set once at week 0 on a player nation is unchanged after 260 weeks. On an AI nation all dials drift to doctrine (tax.lower 0->35, tariff 0->100, admin 30->100, wages 25->85, proc 25->65, edu 90->100, welfare 100->0). The AI never touches the player's budget unless delegation('budget'|'trade') is on; delegation defaults to false (delegation.js emptyDelegation).
measurements.ledger_identity_L9: PASS ON THE HOT PATH - deviation 0.00 for 12 consecutive weeks. BUT L9 is asserted only in ACCOUNTING_INVARIANTS.md and scripts/audit/, never checked in src/, and FOUR refund paths credit the treasury without booking a ledger entry: economy.js dropInvalidProjects 2100 (state branch; the private branch 2097-2099 is correct - asymmetry inside one if/else), recruitment.js cancelTraining 475 (no outlayGold decrement), construction.js cancelConstruction 615-617 (correction clamped at 0 while projectGold is zeroed weekly at 3554), construction.js 906-909 (no correction at all). None fired in the measured window.

tariff.evidence: treasury 2,482 (-15%) -> 53,022 (50%) = 21x; needsMet 0.943 -> 0.700; revenue saturates near 50%. CORRECTION: the tariff does NOT protect domestic industry. settleGlobalTrade() 3310 fixes domestic = min(marketProduction, demand) BEFORE the tariff is read; the tariff only scales the import bid and the export surplus, and producers are paid the bare world price. Factory levels measured 40/39/39/40 across tariff 0..100 - flat. The 32-level outlier is the -15 run whose treasury was drained to 2,482 with a weekly net of -11, so it could not pay construction's hard gold gate. Causal chain is tariff -> treasury -> construction budget, not tariff -> price protection.

tax.middle.evidence: 0 vs 100: middle population 152k -> 105k, satisfaction 0.695 -> 0.431; distinct from the other two only in weight, but the demotion outcome differs MECHANISM IS SHARED: the only middle-specific constants in the whole budget path are the welfare relief rate (economy.js 2582, lower 0.35 / middle 0.12 / upper 0) and the AI tax ceiling (2873, 35/42/45). Everything else is one code path parameterised by a table. Middle is also the only class whose share of the tax base shrinks as the country industrialises (WAGE_SPLIT gives it 0.2 of payroll; all factory profit goes to upper).

militaryWages.evidence: 25 vs 60: army power 47.9 -> 59.3, defence 63.1 -> 78.2, cost 2.25 -> 5.40; in war soldiers 7,906 -> 8,550

militaryProcurement.evidence: 25 vs 60: supplyIndex 0.133 -> 0.228, arms 23.8 -> 27.4; cross-test wages100/proc25 vs wages25/proc100 gives completely different states, so the two are NOT one axis

welfare.evidence: 0 vs 100: lower satisfaction 0.580 -> 0.807, stability 0.544 -> 0.760, GDP 788 -> 843, and the treasury ends HIGHER (56,723 -> 57,880)

education.evidence: 30-year run: literacy 0.195 -> 0.514 (2.6x), research points 2.00 -> 3.57 (+79%), technologies completed 8 -> 9. One extra tech in 30 years for 40% of the treasury and 11% of GDP. Mathematically large, strategically flat. The discrete education GATE (construction.js investmentBlocker 531-536) is the part that matters.

adminFunding.evidence: every non-fiscal outcome byte-identical across 30-100. Marginal revenue 0.45*grossTax = 16.83 vs marginal cost 5.00. 100 is optimal unless gross tax < 11.1/week or population > ~2.9M (measured nation: 919,187).

health.evidence: 0 vs 100: +34 gold/week for +0.66% population over 5 years and zero city growth; standardOfLiving 15.06 -> 17.43

subsidyPolicy.evidence: manual/strategic/none are bit-identical in peacetime (subsidised plants 0, cost 0, GDP 792, treasury 52,404 in all three). Subsidies themselves work: force-marking all plants gives +12% employment, +3.8% GDP for 1.6% of the treasury.

treasury_as_constraint.evidence: held at 0 gold: factory levels 40 -> 24, GDP 792 -> 597. Given +100,000 gold: identical industry, GDP and project count. Peaceful treasuries reach 52k-250k with no sink. With wars enabled over 50 years: 29/29 nations borrowed, 27/29 defaulted, 10.46% of nation-weeks borrowing.

mechanics.one_line: A single anonymous world pool cleared once a week. No partners, no geography, no player decision - the only lever is the tariff, which belongs to Budget.
mechanics.structural_fact: settleGlobalTrade() 3279-3422 never names a counterparty. Exports = surplusCol[i] * crossBorderTrade / totalSurplus (3376); imports = a weighted share of the same crossBorderTrade = min(totalSurplus, totalBid) (3351). Distance, adjacency, coast, ports, sea lanes and blockades are absent from the trade path entirely.

findings.claim: NOT FOUND - conservation is exact

findings.claim: flow.importShare is one week stale where the tariff is charged
findings.proof: set by settleGlobalTrade 3380 in finishEconomy; read by runFactories 2371 and populationDemand 2528 in the NEXT week's runNationEconomy. Deliberate (beginEconomy header documents order-independence) but easy to misread.

findings.claim: A high tariff withholds your own goods from the world pool

findings.claim: The price rule has NO ANCHOR - basePrice appears in updatePrices only as the two clamp arguments, so a price is a pure multiplicative walk that ratchets into a band edge and stays
findings.proof: economy.js 3623 and 3634 are the only uses of basePrice inside updatePrices; grep shows its other uses are the GOODS catalogue, marketGood() 1129-1131 initialisation, priceOf()'s fallback 1336 and a baseCost at 2530. Nothing pulls a price toward base. Measured: 25 of 42 goods already pinned at a band edge by turn 321, 34-38 by turn 5261.

findings.claim: settleGlobalTrade never writes to world.market.goods, so prices cannot learn that trade failed to clear
findings.proof: grep over economy.js 3279-3422 finds exactly one market reference, world.market.hasPriority. The clearing outcome (imports, exports, shortage) never feeds back into price; only the accumulated supply/demand asked for does.

findings.claim: War has no effect on trade whatsoever - two nations in total war supply each other's markets on unchanged terms
findings.proof: settleGlobalTrade 3279-3422 never reads atWar, relations or any diplomatic state (verified by grep over the whole function). No blockade, embargo or wartime premium exists anywhere in src/.

findings.claim: The trade screen's 'World trade' figure is world GDP, not world trade
findings.proof: tradeLedger.js 120 worldTrade: market.totalGdp; updatePrices 3637 sets totalGdp = sum(traded x price) over ALL goods including purely domestic volume

findings.claim: Everything in a week transacts at last week's price, and the price history is itself one week stale
findings.proof: updatePrices runs last in finishEconomy (4000). Within it, 3628-3629 pushes state.price to history BEFORE 3634 updates it, so the sparkline's last plotted point and trendOver(history,36) always describe weeks t-36..t-1.

findings.claim: PRICE_HISTORY is exported to nobody

findings.claim: Four market-state fields plus market.totalGdp are display-only
findings.proof: previousPrice, trend, traded, history and market.totalGdp are read by no file under src/game/ other than updatePrices itself and the tradeLedger/UI layer

findings.claim: Factory input demand is price-blind
findings.proof: runFactories 2363 books requested = inputs * inputScale * laborThroughput regardless of what the input costs, and books it even for the portion the factory cannot afford or receive

findings.claim: The code comments claim 43 goods; GOODS holds 42
findings.proof: comments at economy.js 397, 1209, 1816, 3283 and 3632 say 43; GOOD_IDS.length measured 42 in every run

findings.claim: The fertilizer -> agriculture yield bonus is DEAD: farmBonus is always exactly 1.0
findings.proof: rawProduction 1892-1894 reads fertilizer.demand and .fulfilled, but resetNationGoodsFlow zeroes BOTH (1836, 1841) and runs earlier in the same function (runNationEconomy 3860 vs 3868). The test is always 0 > 0. The reset even preserves the ratio it needs as flow.fulfilledShare at 1844 - rawProduction reads the wrong pair. This is the game's only industry->agriculture link and it has never fired.

findings.claim: Cement demand has no consequence - construction never reads it
findings.proof: runNationEconomy 3931-3932 books cement demand from the build queue every week; grep cement src/game/construction.js returns nothing. Building never slows, stops or costs more for want of cement.

findings.claim: A starved factory bids its full labour-capacity demand forever, pinning the good at the 8x ceiling permanently
findings.proof: runFactories 2359 requested = amount * laborThroughput (labour capacity), not throughput (the input-throttled figure at 2360). Measured at turn 321: fuel at 8x base with production 0.00 and demand 2.25, alongside cement, fertilizer and explosives.

findings.claim: workshopArmsOutput creates small arms from nothing every week - no input, no cost, no market presence
findings.proof: economy.js 725-728 returns 0.08 * (0.5 + militaryProcurement/200); consumed as retainedWorkshop at 3897 and excluded from retainedCost at 3910. A deliberate floor so a nation cannot be permanently unable to field an army, but nothing in the UI says so.

findings.claim: needAmount does NOT grow with the turn - there is no hidden century-long demand inflation
findings.proof: economy.js needAmount() 400-403 is a step function: turn >= need.from ? need.amount : 0. Goods switch on at a threshold; per-capita amounts never scale.

findings.claim: State stockpiling is measured at 0.0% of world demand in peacetime
findings.proof: procureStrategicGoods is the only demand source with a supply gate and switches itself off once stocks reach cap; measured importCost 0 in every peaceful run of the budget matrix and 0.0% of world demand at turns 121/201/401/801

contract.inputs: nation.economy.tariff (owned by Budget); indirectly what the player builds; priorityAccess from companies
contract.outputs: tariffRevenue + settlement into the treasury; inputAvailability into every factory on earth; price into the entire tax base; shortage into needsMet
invariants: sum over nations of trade.importValue == sum of trade.exportValue (measured 0.000000000)
crossBorderTrade == min(totalSurplus, totalBid) and the allocation closes exactly (two passes)
priority access reorders the queue and never creates goods
there is no civilian inventory - unsold output is discarded weekly
settleGlobalTrade never writes world.market.goods - clearing has no same-week price feedback
contract.must_not_write: only addFlow/addNationFlow may write market flows; only updatePrices may write a price; only settleGlobalTrade may write imports/exports/shortage
contract.phase_order: runNationEconomy accumulates supply and demand per nation -> finishEconomy: procureStrategicGoods -> refreshPriorityAccess -> settleGlobalTrade -> updateLedger -> updatePrices. Read a price or an availability only with the knowledge that it is last week's.
